title: APPROVE PERMANENT ORDER AMENDING PORT OF LOS ANGELES TARIFF NO. 4, SECTION THREE, ITEM NO. 370 – “VESSEL TRAFFIC SERVICE USER FEES.”
text:
RESOLUTION NO. ____________ - APPROVE PERMANENT ORDER AMENDING PORT OF LOS ANGELES TARIFF NO. 4, SECTION THREE, ITEM NO. 370 – “VESSEL TRAFFIC SERVICE USER FEES.”
Transmittal 1
Transmittal 2
Transmittal 3
Summary
: Staff requests approval of a Permanent Order to amend Port of Los Angeles (Port) Tariff No. 4 (Tariff), Section Three, Item No. 370 – Vessel Traffic Service User Fees (VTSUF). This request aligns with the portion of the Port of Los Angeles 2026-2030 Strategic Plan that focuses on strong stakeholder relationships. The Marine Exchange of Southern California (MX) operates a Vessel Traffic Service (VTS) that monitors vessel traffic within the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach (the Ports) and in the approaches to the Ports. The VTS provides mariners with timely, relevant, and accurate information to support safe, secure, efficient, reliable, and environmentally sound maritime transportation. The VTSUF classifies vessels into two categories: local and non-local. Local vessels include tugs with commercial tows, passenger ferries to and from Catalina, port construction projects, commercial assistance, whale watching, sport fishing, and support services. These vessels are charged a fixed monthly VTSUF regardless of trip frequency. The current VTSUF for local vessels ranges from $35 per month for commercial assistance vessels to $395 during the summer months for ferries to and from Catalina, with a reduced rate of $195 per month during the winter months. Non-local vessels exceeding 40 meters in length are assessed the VTSUF upon each arrival, regardless of the duration of their stay or the number of movements within port. The VTSUF for these vessels is calculated using a formula with two components based on the vessel’s length overall (LOA) and gross registered tonnage (GRT). The LOA component features seven bands, ranging from $318 for vessels 40-150 meters in length to $675 for those over 335 meters. The GRT component is $0.0043 per GRT. Combining these, the VTSUF per arrival ranges from $320 for the smallest vessel to $1,510 for the largest container ship or tanker. For local vessels, the proposed amendment would increase the VTSUF by 4.0 percent, expanding the current range from $35–$395 per month to $36–$411 per month. The last adjustment to the VTSUF for local vessels occurred in 2021, and the proposed increase would take effect on November 1, 2026. This one-time increase would remain unchanged for the next three years. For non-local vessels, the proposed amendment would increase the VTSUF by 4.0 percent annually over the next three years. In the first year, the current range of $320 to $1,510 per arrival would rise to $333 to $1,649. The VTSUF for non-local vessels was last adjusted in 2023 and is now proposed to increase on November 1, 2026, and on October 1, 2027, and 2028. The VTSUF for non-local entry vessels remains divided into two components: LOA and GRT. Due to increases in vessel size, a new LOA band for vessels over 360 meters is proposed, with the LOA component ranging from $331 to $780, effective November 1, 2026, and subject to a 4% annual increase on October 1, 2027, and 2028. The GRT rate is also proposed to increase by 4% annually—from the current $0.0043 per GRT to $0.0045 on November 1, 2026, to $0.0047 on October 1, 2027, and to $0.0048 in 2028. The overall increase per vessel per arrival would range from $13 to $138, with an average first-year increase of $48 per arrival. Because VTSUF is paid directly to MX, this action has no financial impact on the Harbor Department.
Recommendation
: Board resolve to 1) find that the Director of Environmental Management has determined that the proposed action is statutorily exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Section 15273 of the State CEQA Guidelines; 2) approve the Amendment to the Port of Los Angeles Tariff No. 4, revising Section Three Pilotage, Item No. 370 – Vessel Traffic Service User Fees, subject to the California Association of Port Authorities’ review and approval, and authorize the Executive Director to work with the California Association of Port Authorities to secure this approval or proceed to take independent action in accordance with the California Association of Port Authorities procedure; 3) adopt Permanent Order No.______ with an effective date of November 1, 2026, to amend Section Three Pilotage, Item No. 370, Vessel Traffic Service User Fees in the Port of Los Angeles Tariff No. 4; 4) direct the Board Secretary to transmit to the City Council for approval of the Permanent Order and the Ordinance approving the amendments to the Port of Los Angeles Tariff No. 4 pursuant to City Charter 653(a); 5) direct the Board Secretary to transmit to the City Clerk a Notice of Public Hearing for publication in accordance with the provisions of California Government Code sections 66018 and 6062a; 6) after the effective date of the Ordinance, transmit the Permanent Order and Ordinance to the Executive Director or their nominee for implementation and posting to the Port of Los Angeles website; and 7) adopt Resolution No. __________.
Waterfront & Commercial Real Estate
summary: Approval of Permanent Order amending Port of Los Angeles Tariff No. 4 to increase Vessel Traffic Service User Fees by 4.0 percent annually for three years.
